# pay-agent

An AI agent that autonomously discovers, purchases, and consumes data from x402-protected APIs on Hedera testnet. Every payment is logged to an immutable HCS audit trail.

Submitted for the Hedera x402 Bounty (hedera.com/x402-bounty).

## What x402 Is

x402 is an open payment standard that reuses the HTTP 402 "Payment Required" status code to let servers request payment and clients pay inside ordinary HTTP request/response cycles. It turns payment into something a client can satisfy as easily as following a redirect — no checkout page, account signup, or API-key dance required.

Hedera contributes its own `exact` payment scheme and reference implementation to the official x402 repository (github.com/x402-foundation/x402), so applications and AI agents can settle payments in HBAR or HTS tokens with Hedera's speed and low, predictable fees.

### What x402 IS
- An HTTP-native standard for a single, discrete request → pay → response handshake
- Stateless and per-request — each payment is self-verifying, with no billing session or subscription
- Settlement-agnostic — works across chains and assets; on Hedera it settles in HBAR or HTS tokens
- A shared rulebook so any wallet or service can negotiate value the same way it negotiates data

### What x402 is NOT
- Not a blockchain or a new payment network — it lives on top of existing rails
- Not a custodial processor — facilitators verify and submit, but can never move funds without a signed authorization
- Not for streaming or multi-hop routing — it is optimized for discrete request/response cycles
- Not a general "agentic wallet" — it is one well-scoped primitive, not an autonomy framework

## Real-World Application: Agentic Commerce Infrastructure

AI agents are becoming autonomous economic actors but lack a payment layer. pay-agent builds that layer: per-request micropayments on Hedera (seconds to settle, $0.0001/tx) with immutable audit trails via HCS.

### Use Cases

- **Algorithmic Trading** — Bots buy real-time sentiment, on-chain data, news feeds per-query instead of $10K+/mo subscriptions. HCS satisfies SEC/MiFID II compliance.
- **AI/ML Data Pipeline** — Agents buy training data, inference, specialized APIs. Thousands of $0.001 transactions per day, impossible with credit cards.
- **Research Marketplace** — Researchers sell datasets and papers. Readers pay per access. No accounts, no KYC.
- **Supply Chain & ESG** — Companies buy verified carbon credits and compliance data. HCS creates auditable chain of custody.

## Project Structure

```
packages/server/
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts              # Entry point — registers providers, starts server
│   ├── config.ts             # Environment variable loading
│   ├── hedera.ts             # Hedera client + HCS helpers (create topic, log, query)
│   ├── x402.ts               # Builds x402 paywall from registered providers
│   ├── providers/
│   │   ├── types.ts          # Provider interface definition
│   │   ├── registry.ts       # Dynamic registry + x402 route builder
│   │   ├── weather.ts        # Open-Meteo real API (free, no key)
│   │   ├── market.ts         # CoinGecko real API (free, no key)
│   │   └── compliance.ts     # Tax/regulatory data by jurisdiction
│   ├── routes/
│   │   ├── index.ts          # Aggregates all route modules
│   │   ├── providers.ts      # GET /api/providers — lists available providers
│   │   ├── data.ts           # GET /api/data/:provider — generic data endpoint
│   │   ├── audit.ts          # GET /api/audit — HCS audit trail
│   │   └── chat.ts           # POST /chat — AI agent chat
│   └── tools/
│       └── agent.ts          # LangChain LLM + dynamically built tools from providers
packages/web/
├── src/
│   ├── main.tsx              # React entry point
│   ├── App.tsx               # Dashboard — chat, providers, audit trail
│   └── index.css             # Dark terminal theme
├── index.html
└── vite.config.ts            # Dev proxy to server
```

## Provider System

The core architecture is a **provider registry**. Each data source implements the `Provider` interface:

```typescript
interface Provider {
  slug: string;          // URL segment — e.g. "weather"
  name: string;          // Display name
  description: string;   // What it returns
  price: string;         // Cost per request — e.g. "$0.001"
  params: ProviderParam[];  // Query parameters
  fetch(params: Record<string, string>): Promise<unknown>;  // Real API call
}
```

Providers register in `index.ts`. The x402 paywall, agent tools, and provider listing all build automatically from the registry. Adding a new data source = one file + one `registerProvider()` call.

### Built-in Providers

| Provider | Slug | Price | Upstream API | Real Data? |
|----------|------|-------|-------------|------------|
| Weather | `weather` | $0.001 | Open-Meteo | Yes — geocoding + forecast |
| Crypto Market | `market` | $0.002 | CoinGecko | Yes — live prices, volume, market cap |
| Tax & Compliance | `compliance` | $0.005 | Internal DB | Yes — real tax rates by jurisdiction |

### API Endpoints

- `GET /api/providers` — List all registered providers with params and prices
- `GET /api/data/:provider?param=value` — Fetch data from a provider (behind x402 paywall)
- `GET /api/audit` — Query HCS audit trail for all payment events
- `POST /chat` — AI agent chat (discovers providers, builds tools dynamically)
- `GET /health` — Server health check

## Key Technologies

- x402 protocol (@x402/express, @x402/core, @x402/fetch, @x402/hedera)
- Hedera testnet (hedera:testnet) — HBAR micropayments, ~$0.0001/tx
- Hedera Consensus Service (HCS) — immutable audit trail for every x402 payment
- @hiero-ledger/sdk — native Hedera SDK for HCS topic creation and message submission
- Blocky402 facilitator — open x402 facilitator with Hedera testnet support (no API key)
- Ollama LLM (@langchain/ollama) for agent reasoning
- LangChain — tool orchestration, tools built dynamically from providers

## Hedera Services

| Service | Usage |
|---------|-------|
| Hedera Token Service (HTS) | Native HBAR transfers for x402 micropayments |
| Hedera Consensus Service (HCS) | Immutable log of every payment event to a topic |
| HashScan | Block explorer for verifying transactions and audit logs |

## x402 Flow (Fee-Payer Model)

The Hedera exact scheme uses a fee-payer model where the facilitator pays gas fees and submits transactions:

1. Client requests a protected endpoint (e.g. `GET /api/data/weather?city=Tokyo`)
2. Server responds with HTTP 402 + PaymentRequirements describing cost, asset, payTo, and feePayer
3. Client constructs a Hedera TransferTransaction that moves the requested asset to payTo, sets the feePayer, signs it, and Base64-encodes it into a PaymentPayload
4. Server forwards the payload to the facilitator's /verify endpoint
5. Facilitator validates the transaction structure, asset, amount, and destination
6. Facilitator adds its signature as fee payer, pays the gas, and submits to Hedera via /settle
7. Server responds with data + PAYMENT-RESPONSE receipt
8. HCS audit hook logs the payment event (provider, amount, endpoint, timestamp) to an HCS topic

### PaymentRequirements format:
```json
{
  "scheme": "exact",
  "network": "hedera:testnet",
  "amount": "100000",
  "asset": "0.0.0",
  "payTo": "0.0.12345",
  "maxTimeoutSeconds": 180,
  "extra": {
    "feePayer": "0.0.7162784"
  }
}
```

### PaymentPayload format:
```json
{
  "x402Version": 2,
  "resource": { "url": "/api/data/weather", "description": "..." },
  "accepted": { "scheme": "exact", "network": "hedera:testnet", ... },
  "payload": { "transaction": "AAAAAAAAAAAAA...AAAAAAAAAAAAA=" }
}
```

## Hedera exact Scheme Details

| Property | Detail |
|----------|--------|
| Protocol version | x402Version: 2 |
| Networks | hedera:mainnet, hedera:testnet (CAIP-2 identifiers) |
| Assets | Native HBAR (entity ID 0.0.0) or any HTS fungible token (by entity ID) |
| Amounts | HBAR in tinybars (1 HBAR = 10^8 tinybars); HTS tokens in smallest unit per decimals |
| Fee model | Facilitator acts as feePayer, paying network fees and submitting the transaction |
| Transaction | Direct, partially-signed TransferTransaction (no ScheduleCreate wrapping) |

## HCS Audit Trail

Every x402 payment event is submitted as a message to a dedicated HCS topic. This creates an immutable, timestamped ledger of all agent spending.

Topic message format:
```json
{
  "event": "x402_payment",
  "provider": "weather",
  "endpoint": "/api/data/weather",
  "price": "$0.001",
  "params": { "city": "Tokyo" },
  "timestamp": "2026-07-23T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Query the HCS topic to retrieve the full audit log — verifiable on HashScan.

## Hedera Details

- Network: hedera:testnet
- USDC Token ID: 0.0.429274 (6 decimals)
- HBAR supported as native token (asset ID 0.0.0)
- Blocky402 facilitator: https://api.testnet.blocky402.com (supports hedera:testnet, no API key required)
- Blocky402 fee payer: 0.0.7162784
- Block explorer: https://hashscan.io/testnet
- Facilitator discovery: GET https://api.testnet.blocky402.com/supported

## x402 SDK Reference

Server-side:
- paymentMiddlewareFromConfig() from @x402/express wraps Express routes with x402 paywall
- ExactHederaScheme from @x402/hedera/exact/server for Hedera settlement verification
- x402ResourceServer + HTTPFacilitatorClient from @x402/core/server
- buildX402Routes() from providers/registry.ts generates route config from registered providers

Client-side:
- createClientHederaSigner from @x402/hedera for signing payments with a Hedera private key
- ExactHederaScheme from @x402/hedera/exact/client for client-side signing
- wrapFetchWithPayment from @x402/fetch to auto-handle 402 responses and sign/retry
- x402Client from @x402/core/client to register payment schemes

HCS:
- @hiero-ledger/sdk TopicCreateTransaction to create the audit topic
- @hiero-ledger/sdk TopicMessageSubmitTransaction to log events
- TopicMessageQuery.subscribe() to read back audit entries

## Environment Variables

### packages/server/.env.example
```
HEDERA_ACCOUNT_ID=0.0.12345
HEDERA_PRIVATE_KEY=0x...
HCS_TOPIC_ID=
FACILITATOR_URL=https://api.testnet.blocky402.com
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:3b
PORT=4021
```

### packages/web/.env.example
```
# No env vars needed for local dev — Vite proxies to localhost:4021
VITE_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:4021
```

## Hedera Facilitators

### Blocky402 (recommended for testnet)
- Open x402 facilitator with Hedera support
- Testnet: https://api.testnet.blocky402.com (no API key required)
- Mainnet: rolling out, will require API key
- Fee payer account: 0.0.7162784
- Docs: blocky402.com/docs

### Run your own
x402 is permissionless — any team can operate a facilitator:
1. Implement the exact Hedera scheme using @x402/hedera reference implementation
2. Fund and configure a fee-payer account
3. Expose GET /supported, POST /verify, POST /settle
4. Enforce safety checks (transaction layout, asset exactness, fee-payer safety, replay protection)
